c.tagline: Green, walkable riverside capital where dragons guard the bridges.

taxi.fareNote: Metered within the city; flag-fall around €1.50-2 plus roughly €1-1.30/km. Always confirm the meter is running or agree a fixed price up front, especially for airport transfers, as some unlicensed drivers overcharge tourists.

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU emergency number for ambulance/fire; 113 reaches police directly.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Occasional pickpocketing in the busy Old Town and Central Market in summer — otherwise a very safe city.

hood_desc: The pedestrianized historic core along the Ljubljanica River with the Triple Bridge, Prešeren Square and Ljubljana Castle above; best for first-timers who want to walk everywhere, though it's the priciest, busiest area.
A gritty, creative district anchored by the Metelkova alternative-culture squat and indie bars, popular with younger travelers and hostel-goers who want nightlife within an easy walk of downtown.
A picturesque, low-key residential quarter along the Gradaščica canal with artsy cafes and a weekend market, ideal for travelers wanting a quieter, local feel just south of the center.
A leafy, more business-oriented district north of downtown near Tivoli Park and the Stožice sports complex, suited to those wanting quieter streets, good value, and easy bus access to the center.
A residential, university-adjacent area southwest of downtown near the zoo and Tivoli Park's edge, offering good-value stays for travelers with a car or prioritizing budget over a central location.

water.note: Excellent, EU-compliant tap water straight from protected springs; public fountains even offer free drinking water.

transit.pay: Fares run on the reloadable Urbana smart card, tapped on validators when boarding; the card (and a small deposit) is bought and topped up at kiosks, the Tourist Info Center, LPP points of sale, or the Urbana app, and single cash tickets are not sold on the bus. One tap covers a flat-fare ride regardless of distance, with free transfers within a set time window.
transit.hours: Most city buses run about 5:00/5:30 AM to 10:30/11:30 PM; a limited night-bus network covers a few core routes into the early hours on weekends.
transit.note: The old town center is compact and largely pedestrianized, and free electric Kavalir shuttles ferry visitors around it on request.

train: Ljubljana railway station, with connections to Vienna, Zagreb, Munich, Budapest and Venice
bus: Ljubljana Bus Station (Avtobusna postaja Ljubljana) for domestic and international coaches

transit.m: Public bus route 28 to city center bus/train station (~45 min)

tip.r: Rounding up or adding roughly 5-10% for good service is appreciated but not expected; service charges are not added to bills.

landmarks: Ljubljana Castle
A medieval hilltop fortress overlooking the city, reachable by funicular, offering sweeping views, a watchtower, and centuries of Slovenian history to explore.
Triple Bridge (Tromostovje)
Architect Jože Plečnik's ingenious trio of pedestrian bridges spanning the Ljubljanica River, forming one of the most photographed and beloved spots in the old town.
Dragon Bridge (Zmajski most)
An Art Nouveau bridge guarded by four bronze dragon statues, the whimsical symbol of Ljubljana and one of its most iconic photo opportunities.
Prešeren Square
The lively heart of Ljubljana's old town, framed by the pink Franciscan Church and a statue of beloved poet France Prešeren, buzzing day and night.
Ljubljana Cathedral (St. Nicholas)
A baroque green-domed cathedral near the riverside market, famed for its ornate bronze doors and dazzling ceiling frescoes depicting Slovenian saints.
Ljubljanica River Embankments
Willow-lined riverside promenades packed with cafes and market stalls, best explored by a leisurely boat ride or an evening stroll beneath the old bridges.
Tivoli City Park
Ljubljana's largest green space, a landscaped park with grand promenades, gardens, and a hilltop mansion, offering a peaceful escape from the compact old town.
National and University Library
A masterpiece by architect Jože Plečnik, its dramatic dark stone facade and grand staircase make it one of the most striking modernist buildings in Europe.
Ljubljana Central Market
Another Plečnik design, this riverside market's colonnades and open-air stalls brim with fresh produce, flowers, and local delicacies, forming a daily social hub.
Metelkova Mesto
A former army barracks turned vibrant alternative art squat, covered in murals and sculptures, offering an edgy contrast to Ljubljana's tidy baroque core.

train.note: All services leave from Ljubljana's single main station, immediately next to the bus station and a 10-minute walk from the old town. The overnight sleeper and couchette cars to Zurich and Stuttgart depart together around 22:10 and split en route, so make sure you board the right carriage. Slovenia and Croatia are both in Schengen now, so there is no routine passport check on the Zagreb train, but keep ID handy. There are also direct trains to Rijeka twice a day and a summer weekend direct service to Pula in Istria; domestic tickets are cheapest bought at the station rather than from abroad.

bus.note: Long-distance coaches use Avtobusna postaja Ljubljana, the main bus station directly in front of the railway station, where each operator has a window and there is a joint departures board. Nomago covers most Slovenian and near-border routes including the coast at Piran and Portoroz, while FlixBus handles the longer runs to Vienna, Munich, Venice and Zagreb. Buy online for the international routes; domestic and Croatian-coast tickets can usually be bought at the counter on the day.

ferry.note: Ljubljana is inland with no ferries; in summer, boats do run from Slovenia's short stretch of coast about 120 km away, where Liberty Lines operates a seasonal fast ferry between Piran and Trieste and day catamarans link Piran with Venice.

half.name: Lake Bled
half.blurb: Iconic alpine lake with an island church and clifftop castle framed by mountains.

half.name: Postojna Cave
half.blurb: Vast karst cave system explored partly by train, filled with dramatic stalactites and rare olms.

half.name: Lake Bohinj
half.blurb: Larger, quieter glacial lake set within Triglav National Park amid soaring alpine peaks.

half.name: Vintgar Gorge
half.blurb: Scenic gorge with wooden walkways hugging turquoise river rapids, pools, and waterfalls.

half.name: Predjama Castle
half.blurb: Dramatic Renaissance castle built into the mouth of a cliff cave, often paired with Postojna.

half.name: Piran
half.blurb: Charming Venetian-flavored seaside town with narrow streets, a harbor, and Adriatic views.
